criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists), strong need justification with cited literature (NOAA, NatGeo, Nature). Requirements not formally stated, but concept and rationale are complete and well referenced.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with weekly tasks, deadlines and task descriptions tied to mission stages (launch, orbit, ground, comms). However, no explicit contingency provision, and the orbit plan contains a significant technical error (see technical issues), weakening plan credibility.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is modest: literature research on bleaching detection and completion of four STK tutorials, but no preliminary results, calculations, or orbit/coverage outputs are presented or interpreted.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings, readable and well-written prose, labelled Gantt figure with legend. But references are bare URLs as footnotes rather than proper citations, report is very short (~2 pages), and no figure caption for Image 1.

technical_issues.issue: 'My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km, which keeps the satellite fixed above the reef' — geostationary orbit is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO and cannot be geostationary or fixed over the reef.

A single geostationary satellite would also give poor resolution for reef-scale colour/bathymetry sensing; mission concept implies imaging needs a LEO constellation — inconsistency between concept and orbit choice.
References given as raw URLs rather than cited properly; no formal requirements derived from user needs.

overall: Strong, well-referenced mission concept for GBR monitoring with clear users and need. Gantt-based plan is detailed but lacks contingencies and contains a major orbit error (600 km 'geostationary'). Preliminary progress (tutorials, research) is modest with no results. Presentation is clear but references are bare URLs.

feedback.summary: Strong, well-referenced mission concept for Great Barrier Reef bleaching monitoring with clear users and need. Your Gantt-based plan is detailed but lacks contingencies and contains a major orbit error (600 km 'geostationary'). Preliminary progress is modest — tutorials and research only, with no technical results. Presentation is clear, but references are bare URLs rather than proper citations.
next_steps: Correct the orbit description: geostationary orbits are ~35,786 km; a 600 km orbit is LEO and cannot remain fixed over the reef. Reconcile your orbit choice with the imaging resolution your reef-monitoring concept implies (likely a LEO constellation).
Add explicit contingency provisions to your project plan (e.g. buffer time, fallback tasks) and explain why the plan is structured this way in the context of the mission.
Present preliminary technical results from your STK work — e.g. orbit parameters, coverage or revisit-time outputs — with brief interpretation, not just a list of completed tutorials.
Replace bare-URL footnotes with proper in-text citations matched to a reference list, and add a caption for your Gantt chart figure.
Derive formal mission requirements (e.g. spatial resolution, revisit rate, latency) explicitly from the identified user needs.

criteria.C1: Your mission concept and rationale are clear and complete: GBR bleaching monitoring, explicit users (marine and conservation scientists), and strong need justification supported by cited literature (NOAA, Nature, NatGeo). To consolidate the Accomplished level, state formal mission requirements derived from user needs rather than leaving them implicit.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart with weekly tasks, deadlines and stage-based descriptions is detailed and credible. However, there is no provision for contingencies or variations, and the plan contains a significant technical error — describing a 600 km orbit as geostationary — which weakens credibility. Fixing the orbit description and adding contingency planning would lift this to Accomplished.
criteria.C3: You have completed four STK tutorials and useful literature research on bleaching detection, but no preliminary results, calculations, or orbit/coverage outputs are presented or interpreted. The Accomplished level requires a good preliminary set of results with brief description and interpretation, showing you are clearly on track.
criteria.C4: Your report is well structured with clear headings, readable prose, and a labelled Gantt chart with legend. However, references are bare URLs as footnotes rather than proper citations, the report is very short (~2 pages), and Image 1 lacks a caption. Consistent, properly formatted citations and fuller development would reach Accomplished.
